answer: In an agent economy buying glacier forecasts and mesa surveys, a public randomness beacon assigns paid jobs with probability proportional to each agent's locked stake. Stake stays locked for the entire job round, so the same coins cannot back multiple entries. Splitting 100 coins across a thousand fake agents gives no more expected work than staking 100 coins under one identity. To capture more jobs, an attacker must lock more capital and forgo its use elsewhere.
